title: Co-optimization for Adaptive Conformal Prediction
claim: Fixed equal-tailed intervals are displaced under skew; folding and balancing endpoint densities moves any interval to the shortest, highest-density one.
layout: 4 panels in 2x2 grid, reading a→d, density plots with push-pull arrows
description: A 2x2 grid of density plots that builds an intuition for how an interval is moved toward the highest-density interval (HDI). (a) shows a right-skewed density f(y|x) with a purple conformal (CQR) interval and its center m. A teal HDI is shaded over it and sits shifted to the left of the CQR interval. (b) folds the left side of the density around a purple vertical line at m onto the right side, giving a two-layer curve in blue (folded) and red (right side). (c) shows the folded distribution as a function of |y-m|, with a vertical quantile line, labeled points A and B, hatched tail masses, and a blue 'Push' arrow and a red 'Pull' arrow. (d) shows the end state, where A and B meet at equal density and m is the HDI center. Purple marks the CQR/initial center, teal marks the HDI, and blue and red mark the two sides.
caption: From any interval to HDI via folding and boundary balancing. (a) Under skewness, equaltailed intervals can be displaced relative to the HDI and are typically longer. (b) Folding around a candidate center m maps y to |y −m|, producing a two-layer view. (c) The folded (1 −α)-boundary corresponds to two endpoints; translating m shortens the interval when the endpoint densities are imbalanced (push–pull). (d) At equilibrium the endpoint densities match, recovering the HDI.
abstract: In regression, conformal prediction often suffers from inefficiency under heteroscedasticity and skewness due to fixed, non-adaptive interval centering. We propose CoCP, a new method that parameterizes prediction intervals by a center $m(x)$ and a radius $h(x)$, and alternates between learning $h(x)$ via smooth quantile regression on folded residuals and refining $m(x)$ using a smooth interval loss. This corrects mis-centering and drives the interval toward high-density regions. Beyond finite-sample marginal validity via split-conformal calibration, we prove that CoCP also attains asymptotic conditional coverage and optimal interval length if the base estimators are consistent. Experiments demonstrate that CoCP yields tighter intervals and achieves improved empirical conditional-coverage reliability. Code is available at https://github.com/jjoeysu/cocp.
